correctness.rationale: Reconstructed every case of the strict-convex local increment lemma: noncollinear increments by strict triangle, unequal positive multiples by independent perturbation, opposite multiples by parallel perturbation, and zero by the opposite direction. For complex L1, a finite-measure threshold set, countable dense perturbations, and signed measurable localization produce a nonzero integral. No finite experiment is substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: The result isolates the previously untreated endpoint ℓ1 across arbitrary families of strictly convex blocks, establishing the exact necessary/sufficient scalar-dimension threshold. The 2013 Theorem A supplies the germ equivalence, its Proposition 6 covers real L1, and its mixed ℓ1/ℓ2 construction does not give the full ℓ1 classification. The 2026 theorem is stronger on nonatomic Bochner L1 but does not classify atomic ℓ1-sums by real one-dimensional multiplicity. The previous ℓp (1<p<∞) sum result cannot imply the ℓ1 endpoint. A hidden equivalent general sum statement remains a real residual risk.
residual_risks: Undiscovered historical literature could state an equivalent geometric classification of flat local norm germs for absolute sums.
The strict-convexity hypothesis is essential to the proof; no general criterion for merely (S) component spaces is established.
The complex L1 nonatomic case is already a corollary of a stronger published uniform-(S) theorem and carries no standalone originality claim.

value.rationale: An exact structural threshold separates preservation from failure of a non-strictly-convex Steinhaus property for all index cardinalities at the ℓ1 endpoint. It explains why ℓ1 sums of Hilbert planes and complex scalar fibers behave differently from two real lines, identifies the minimal obstruction, and completes a natural closure classification left outside the prior 1<p<∞ sum theorem; the claim is not a renaming or arbitrary finite parameter slice.
